contact_edits.before: Ever Yours, Oscar has been devised by Peter Wylde; Bedford directs himself. It doesn't pretend to be a play, and it's fragmentary even as a recital. Bedford reads or speaks at a music stand, placed about three quarters of the way upstage (anyone sitting behind in this three-handed space will have only his back to look at) with a large portrait of Wilde hanging on the back wall. In between epistles, he delivers snippets of basic biography. The Sturm und Drang of Wilde's life are given bare-bones treatment; we hear very little of, or to, Bosie, though what we do hear makes him sound more appalling than ever. There's nothing from the anguished De Profundis, technically a letter but hardly an informal one. Basically, the show gives us sidelights, mainly delightful ones; ranging from the young Oscar admonishing his mother on what to send him at prep school to the enfant terrible Oscar on his lecture tour of the United States, instructing silver miners on the subject of modern art. (They hated the art, loved the artist -- i. e. him.) In short --and it is short -- this is not a momentous evening or, preferably, afternoon. But it offers insights, and one of our very finest actors being very fine. - Ever Yours, Oscar is in repertory through Aug. 29. Visit stratfordfestival.ca or call 1-800-567-1600 for tickets and information.
